subject: ClinicCore: DPA and technical evidence for PHI handling
messages:
From: security@cliniccore.com
To: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@cliniccore.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request for DPA and PHI handling evidence for RFP

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our RFP intake we need: a copy of your Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with any standard redlines accepted, a concise description of how PHI is ingested/processed/stored by Redwood when integrated via your hosted API, and high-level evidence items (SOC 2 type II report, dataflow diagram, KMS/HSM usage notes).

Attached is Appendix A from our RFP that lists required artifacts. Can you confirm what you can provide within 5 business days? Also flag anything that would require legal review or an addendum.

Appreciate it,

Samantha Lee
Security Program Manager
ClinicCore Health
security@cliniccore.com

Attachment: ClinicCore_RFP_Appendix_A.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
To: security@cliniccore.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-02T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for DPA and PHI handling evidence for RFP

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending Appendix A and for the clear list. We can provide the following within 3 business days, and we’ve attached a concise DPA response doc to start:

- Draft DPA response and standard Redwood DPA (see attached PDF)
- High-level dataflow diagram showing PHI ingress, in-memory processing, and encrypted-at-rest storage (attached PNG)
- KMS/HSM configuration summary (attached TXT)
- Current SOC 2 Type II report — we will share via secure link once we confirm your tokenized access (security requirement)

Key clarifications up front:
- Our hosted API does not persist user-submitted prompt text to long-term storage by default; ephemeral caches are used for in-flight inference and are purged per retention policy unless a customer has opted into logging for analytics.
- When customers enable logging/analytics, PHI can be routed to a customer-dedicated bucket that is encrypted with a per-customer KMS key.
- For high-volume regulated deployments we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated pools — we can put those options in the RFP response.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_Response_20260902.pdf, end-to-end-dataflow-diagram.png, KMS-configuration-summary.txt

Next steps: If you’re open, I’d propose a 45-minute technical Q&A early next week (we can bring product, infra, and legal). Proposed slots: Tue 9/8 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 9/9 14:00–14:45 PT.

Best,

Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0182

From: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
To: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-02T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: ClinicCore: DPA and technical evidence for PHI handling — suggested redlines

Logan — forwarding for awareness. I reviewed the DPA response PDF and drafted a redline focused on retention, subprocessor disclosures, and KMS key ownership options. Suggested bullets to call out in the reply:

- Retention defaults: 30 days for ephemeral inference caches; ability to opt into 90/365 day retention for analytics with explicit customer consent
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; per-customer KMS keys available for Dedicated and Private deployments
- Key ownership: Redwood-managed KMS by default; customer-managed keys (CMKs) supported via KMS in Dedicated and Private
- Subprocessors: list of infra providers (GCP us-west2, S3 buckets with SSE-KMS, internal inference fleet vendors) — recommend we attach an ASP list rather than inline in email

I attached a working redline doc (DPA_Redline_ClinicCore_v2.docx). Marissa, can you skim the clause language on liability caps and BAA addendum — ClinicCore tends to push on retention and deletion evidence.

Thanks — M

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-02T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClinicCore DPA redline — legal suggestions

Thanks Monica — quick notes from legal:

- Retention & Deletion: Accept the 30-day default but add documented deletion verification process for PHI (audit log + job id). We can provide a deletion certificate on request for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Liability / Indemnity: Aim to keep indemnity focused on Redwood breaches caused by Redwood negligence; do NOT accept broad customer indemnities for customer-provided data processing choices.
- KMS: Approve offering CMK option but require an implementation appendix when CMK is selected (to capture key rotation/backup responsibilities).
- SOC 2: We will share a redacted SOC 2 report via secure link; include statement that full report is available under NDA.

I'll attach a short FAQ on KMS and HSM patterns that we can share with ClinicCore (legal_kms_faq.txt). Logan — once you confirm the meeting slot I'll join the Q&A to handle legal/RFP questions live.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: security@cliniccore.com
To: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@cliniccore.com
Date: 2026-09-04T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClinicCore: DPA and technical evidence for PHI handling

Logan / Monica / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the documents. A couple of follow-ups before the Q&A:

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood ever persists PHI to long-term storage in the hosted offering unless explicitly enabled by the customer?
2) Please provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II (we’ll sign the short confidentiality agreement) and the end-to-end dataflow diagram in a higher-res format.
3) We’d like the CMK appendix language in the DPA redline to show responsibilities for key rotation and emergency key recovery.

Meeting: Tue 9/8 10:00–10:45 PT works for our team. Please send a calendar invite with dial-in and a shared doc we can use to track action items.

Best,

Samantha Lee
Security Program Manager | ClinicCore Health
security@cliniccore.com
